newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK provisional October M0.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK provisional October M0.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing October M0 money supply rose 0.7 percent m-m and 7.5 percent y-y vs expected 0.5 percent and 7.1 percent respectively.
"UK M0 growth in October is consistent with an accelerating trend in consumer spending and will increase the likelihood of the Bank of England calling for more rate hikes."

"It's slightly stronger than the market was looking for. Overall it supports the idea that retail activity will remain fairly strong. The 7.5 percent is a robust figure, well above the government's monitoring range, but it has been for some time. It supports the idea that the recovery is going to continue. It's slightly negative for the market at the short end."

"The M0 figure will not be liked by the gilt market given it's already fearful of further interest rate hikes, but it will do sterling's prospects no harm at all. The further pick-up in the trend rate of M0 growth provides additional support for the view that consumer spending will remain firm. I expect the CBI distributive trades survey due later this week to further underline the message in this M0 data."
